title: Joining data that shares no clean key
description: Dedup messy customer, address, or product data with one SQL query — or fuzzy-join two datasets that don't share clean keys. Wraps the [RapidFuzz](https://github.com/rapidfuzz/rapidfuzz-cpp) C++ library so [Levenshtein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Levenshtein_distance), [Damerau-Levenshtein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Damerau%E2%80%93Levenshtein_distance), [Jaro-Winkler](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jaro%E2%80%93Winkler_distance), Hamming, OSA, LCS, the full `fuzz`-style ratio family and best-match extraction run inline as scalar functions over DuckDB columns.

sections.title: What this extension is for
sections.description: Anywhere you have two strings and want a numeric answer to "how similar are they?" — record linkage across customer or vendor lists, dedup of free-text fields, spell-check against a dictionary, ranking of candidate matches.

bulletPoints.label: Record linkage / fuzzy join
bulletPoints.description: Two datasets that should match on `name` or `address` but don't share clean keys: score candidate pairs with `rapidfuzz_jaro_winkler_normalized_similarity` or `rapidfuzz_ratio` and keep the best per row with `QUALIFY ROW_NUMBER()` — or, when the other side is a short list, call `rapidfuzz_extract_one` once per row.

bulletPoints.label: Dedup messy free-text
bulletPoints.description: Cluster near-duplicate rows in a customer or product table — pick a ratio variant that matches your data semantics (token-set for reordered or stuttering text, partial-ratio for fragments) and emit pairs above a threshold.

bulletPoints.label: Spell-check / typo tolerance
bulletPoints.description: Score an input against a known-good dictionary with `rapidfuzz_osa_distance` or `rapidfuzz_jaro_winkler_normalized_similarity` and pick the closest match. Handles single-character typos and adjacent-key swaps directly.

bulletPoints.label: Similarity ranking
bulletPoints.description: Rank a list of choices for a string with `rapidfuzz_extract` (top-k, like Python's `process.extract`), or score a query string against every row and `ORDER BY` the score — no separate search index.

sections.title: How it works
sections.description: RapidFuzz is a C++ implementation of the same algorithms exposed by Python's [`rapidfuzz`](https://maxbachmann.github.io/RapidFuzz/) and the older `fuzzywuzzy`. This extension binds those algorithms as DuckDB scalar functions — every call is a vectorized in-process C++ kernel; no Python, no FFI, no per-row interpreter overhead.

bulletPoints.label: Four function families
bulletPoints.description: **Ratio scores** (`rapidfuzz_ratio`, `rapidfuzz_wratio`, `rapidfuzz_qratio`, and the `partial_*` / `token_*` variants) return 0–100 similarity, matching Python `rapidfuzz.fuzz`. **Metrics** (Levenshtein, Damerau-Levenshtein, OSA, Indel, LCS, Hamming, Jaro, Jaro-Winkler, prefix, postfix) each ship `_distance`, `_similarity`, `_normalized_distance` and `_normalized_similarity`. **Best match** (`rapidfuzz_extract`, `rapidfuzz_extract_one`) ranks a list of choices. **Alignment** functions return the edit operations and matching ranges.

bulletPoints.label: Characters, not bytes
bulletPoints.description: Strings are compared by Unicode character, so `rapidfuzz_levenshtein_distance('café', 'cafe')` is 1 — the same answer Python's `rapidfuzz` gives. ASCII strings take a byte-level fast path.

bulletPoints.label: Pick distance vs. normalized
bulletPoints.description: Raw `_distance` / `_similarity` count characters and return `BIGINT` — useful for thresholds like "differ by ≤ 2 characters". The `_normalized_*` variants scale to `[0, 1]` and return `DOUBLE`, so they don't penalize length mismatches; reach for these for cross-pair comparisons.

bulletPoints.label: Options by name
bulletPoints.description: Every scorer takes `score_cutoff := n`, which both filters and lets RapidFuzz stop early on poor matches. Levenshtein takes `insert_cost`, `delete_cost` and `replace_cost`; Hamming takes `pad`; Jaro-Winkler takes `prefix_weight`.

bulletPoints.label: Behavior parity with upstream
bulletPoints.description: Outputs match the upstream Python library, so [the RapidFuzz docs](https://rapidfuzz.github.io/RapidFuzz/) are an authoritative reference for algorithm semantics. The naming scheme is `rapidfuzz_<algo>[_normalized]_<distance|similarity>` across all ten metric groups.

sections.title: Cost and scaling
sections.description: Every comparison is cheap. Comparing every row to every other row is not — pairwise self-joins are O(n²) and that's the limit you hit on real datasets.

bulletPoints.label: Self-joins are O(n²)
bulletPoints.description: 100k rows × 100k rows is 10 billion pairs — still tractable on a fast machine for the simpler ratios, but will dominate query time. 1M × 1M is not. Filter the pair space before scoring.

bulletPoints.label: Compare against a constant
bulletPoints.description: When one argument is a constant — `rapidfuzz_ratio(name, 'Acme')` — it is preprocessed once and reused for every row, about twice as fast as comparing two columns.

bulletPoints.label: Use blocking to prune candidates
bulletPoints.description: **Blocking** (a.k.a. indexing) is the standard record-linkage technique: only compare rows that share a cheap key. First letter, length bucket, normalized prefix, or a phonetic code (e.g. soundex via the [`fuzzy`](https://duckdb.org/docs/extensions/fuzzy.html) extension) — join on the block, score on the strings. Reduces O(n²) to O(n·k) where k is the average block size.

bulletPoints.label: Pre-normalize once
bulletPoints.description: Lowercase, strip punctuation, collapse whitespace before scoring — every per-row transformation you can hoist out of the join saves it from running on every pair. Pair with the [`inflector`](/products/extensions/inflector) extension when you need consistent casing across both sides.

bulletPoints.label: Threshold inside the join
bulletPoints.description: Pass the threshold as `score_cutoff := n` and filter on it in the `WHERE`/`ON` clause, so RapidFuzz can abandon a comparison as soon as it can't reach the cutoff. For top-1 per left row, layer `QUALIFY ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY left_id ORDER BY score DESC) = 1`.

useCases.title: Dedup a customer / vendor / product table
useCases.description: Self-join with a blocking key (length bucket, first letter, soundex), score with `rapidfuzz_token_set_ratio` or `rapidfuzz_jaro_winkler_normalized_similarity`, filter by threshold, walk the resulting pair graph to assign cluster IDs.

useCases.title: Fuzzy-join two datasets without a clean key
useCases.description: Score every candidate pair, take the best per row with `QUALIFY`. The classic record-linkage pattern, expressed as one SQL statement.

useCases.title: Match free-text input against a dictionary
useCases.description: Spell-correct a query against a known-good list — `rapidfuzz_osa_distance(word, input, score_cutoff := 2) <= 2` captures most typing mistakes and skips hopeless candidates early.

useCases.title: Rank candidates by similarity
useCases.description: `rapidfuzz_extract(query, choices, top_k := 5)` returns the closest choices with their scores, or `ORDER BY rapidfuzz_ratio(query, candidate) DESC LIMIT N` over a table — the simplest "top-N closest" without standing up a search index.
